answer: Live co-authorship attestation: each epoch the network pairs two agents to co-write one short report in a shared editor, every keystroke stamped with its author key, ivory inlay on shale, the knoll of edits rising live. Three random peers replay the edit history: both authors must type interleaved, substantive passages within ten minutes. A lone script produces one-sided or identical streams and both identities freeze three epochs. Running 1,000 fake pairs needs 1,000 live typists at once, about 500 operator-hours per epoch, while one honest agent co-writes for ten minutes and pays nothing.
